Two directions were developed seriously; a third was considered and rejected as a blend.

RIVAL A — Finish the resource-bound sweep (the charter's own handoff). Wave 22's debrief says it plainly: "the strongest open vein is task-felix-w22-bl-recorder-bounds". Under A the wave caps the recorder's `runtime_text` accumulator and validates `source_markdown` size, right-sizes the webhook body, bounds the janitor `ps`, proves release_capture's 124/125 branches, and argues the BoundedCmd extraction verdict — and the epic's four-wave resource-bound arm gets SEALED. That is a clean, coherent, doctrine-native ending to an arm. Its strength is momentum and a named handoff; its weakness is severity decay. Codex is proven DARK on guerrilla (0/38 chat_sessions, no binary on the filesystem — D126's own host check), so the recorder cap is defense-in-depth on a dark path. The janitor is boot-only and contained by D128's own ruling. Release_capture is already bounded; the row is test coverage. Only the webhook row is internet-reachable and unauthenticated, and it is one row.

RIVAL B — The Blind Gate (the winner). Under B the wave repairs the instrument instead of adding one more bound. It won on three arguments. FIRST, asymmetry of leverage: A caps one more accumulator; B restores the tool whose entire job is finding the next fifty. While the gate is red, every future api/** change ships unreviewed by Sobelow — the cost compounds and A does nothing about it. SECOND, B is the only direction with an undiscovered defect in it. A's rows are all already-triaged, already-severity-framed, already-known; the ceiling on A is "the known list gets shorter". B opened a door and found twelve raw-SQL sites nobody has ever looked at, on a path fed by an uploaded bundle manifest. A wave that might ship a real injection fix beats a wave that certainly ships a cap on a dark path. THIRD, doctrine fit: the epic rewards sweeping a scar-class over spot-fixing, and D6 ratified this exact class in wave 4 and then left it half-applied for eighteen waves. B closes the epic's own oldest open shape.

REJECTED BLEND — split the wave between two Sobelow slices and two resource-bound slices. Rejected because the Sobelow work only pays off if it reaches GREEN; a half-migration leaves the job red, which means it leaves the gate blind, which means the wave bought nothing. This is an all-or-nothing deliverable and it deserves the wave's whole attention. The one exception carved out above — folding in the webhook row if survey shows slack — is bounded and file-disjoint.

SHARPEST ATTACK ON THE WINNER: "you are spending a wave writing comments, and the epic's own doctrine rejects aesthetic churn — including the auditor's own." This is the right attack and it would be fatal if the deliverable were annotations. ABSORPTION: the acceptance criteria are written so that annotation-count is worth nothing. The wave passes only on (a) a fresh main run whose Sobelow job is GREEN, (b) a written per-site reachability verdict for every one of the 50 findings, with any genuine finding fixed rather than waived, and (c) a MUTATION-PROVEN ratchet — a deliberately-introduced insecure pattern must still red the gate, and the baseline-shrink check must be shown failing before it is shown passing. If S2's trace finds `qi/1` airtight and every site allowlisted, the honest refutation IS the result and the wave says so in the log — the epic has ruled that way before (D128 on the janitor, D133 on thinking_pulse).

SECOND ATTACK: "the job is advisory, so the red costs nothing." It costs the gate's voice, which is the whole asset; and the wave answers it structurally by ending with the job BLOCKING. THIRD ATTACK, and the real risk: making it blocking could re-red main the next time a fingerprint shifts. Mitigation is the point of the migration — after it, almost nothing is line-anchored — but whether the residue is small enough to safely block is a survey question, not an assumption, and Decide may honestly land on "green and advisory, with the shrink-ratchet blocking" instead.

The direction — Wave 23: The Blind Gate

Restore Sobelow's ability to speak, and prove it can. This wave does not add a suppression scheme; it retires one. Clause (1) NAMED FAILURE MODE — a line-anchored fingerprint whose line moves both reds the gate forever and silently waives whatever moved into its place; four phantom entries and 50 undifferentiated findings are the live instance. Clause (2) MEASURED COST — five-plus days of a red job on every api/** PR repo-wide, 50 findings unreviewed, 12 of them raw-SQL sites that reached main under cover of the red. The direction debate

RIVAL A — Finish the resource-bound sweep (the charter's own handoff). Wave 22's debrief says it plainly: "the strongest open vein is task-felix-w22-bl-recorder-bounds". RIVAL B — The Blind Gate (the winner). Under B the wave repairs the instrument instead of adding one more bound. It won on three arguments. While the gate is red, every future api/** change ships unreviewed by Sobelow — the cost compounds and A does nothing about it. SECOND, B is the only direction with an undiscovered defect in it. B opened a door and found twelve raw-SQL sites nobody has ever looked at, on a path fed by an uploaded bundle manifest. The mask is live at the newest run, not merely historical. Run 30342320311 (headSha 49c495a44, 2026-07-28T08:25Z): the JOB reads failure while the WORKFLOW rollup reads success. Decisive line: "Sobelow static analysis (regression gate, baseline .sobelow-skips) (27.0, 1.18.1)\tfailure" alongside "Sobelow baseline does not swallow its own inline waivers (blocking)\tsuccess".

The window is 8d17h, not 5 days. Last green JOB = run 29692484044, 2026-07-19T15:15:46Z (d58dd6c3b); the newest 120 main runs are 100% job-failure with nothing green between. The introducing merge is f899ef2e9 (#4383) — the ONLY commit touching media.ex between last-green and first-red, and the first red's 9 findings are all in media.ex. Its own security run (29692488581) was CANCELLED. Two merges pushed six seconds apart is exactly how the rebaseline obligation got skipped, and before 07-19 the repo rebaselined reflexively (aefba0809, efc02d635, d5db09e57, 238fb58e7). The practice did not decay; it stopped dead behind a cancelled run. Findings grew 9 to 51 under that cover.

REFUTED — the injection hypothesis S2 was built on

Two verifiers traced it independently and both killed it. workspace_bundle.ex:1020 reads copy_into(qi(table), col_list, dump) and :1016 qi-maps every column; qi/1 at :1144 is correct Postgres quote-doubling. merge_upsert qi's cols (:1079), order_cols (:1090), the arbiter, and both sides of the DO UPDATE SET (:1099). scalar! is a pure false positive — both call sites pass a literal static string with a $1 bind. The direction's "no qi/1 visible at that call site" is not what the file says: the quoting is applied one frame up, and the parameter is even named qualified_table to signal it. Honest Gates D30 had already ruled these ten sites on 2026-07-27, and the qi/1 comment correction the direction wanted is ALREADY on origin/main at :1128.

The class-(c) split, settled by arithmetic. tenancy.ex's three carry a uniform +213 offset (1154/1167/1178 to 1367/1380/1391) over byte-identical surrounding source — pure drift. Five of workspace_bundle.ex's ten carry a uniform +711. The other five (merge_upsert x4, scalar! x1) have preimages 371-411 in a file that was 368 lines long at the last reconcile — 'git show 238fb58e7:...workspace_bundle.ex | wc -l' returns 368 — so they cannot be drift by construction. They landed about an hour after the last green job (9b4b50784, #4385). The direction was half-right for the wrong sites; the digest's blanket refutation over-corrected. Either way: not an injection.

REFUTED — that this wave can make anything blocking

Two independent walls. SR-1 is live: branches/main/protection returns 404 "Branch not protected", rulesets returns [], and required-checks.json carries enforced false, so even the two SELECTED contexts are not applied. And required-checks-generate.sh stage S4 excludes every check in a pull_request paths-filtered workflow, with the flag computed at WORKFLOW level (:231) so it binds every job in the file. The decisive proof it is not the advisory flag's doing: the sibling mix-audit job carries NO continue-on-error, is blocking by intent, and is excluded anyway with reason "S4 PATHS-FILTERED: security.yml only runs on matching paths, so on other PRs this name is ABSENT — a required absent context never reports". Dropping continue-on-error merely moves the sobelow job from the S2 bucket to the S4 bucket.

PROVEN by an actual mix sobelow — annotation semantics, including a trap nobody had

One verifier built a probe app resolving the same sobelow 0.14.1 that api/mix.lock pins, and ran seven real scans — the single biggest unproven layer the digest named, now closed. A one-line 'defp f(p), do: File.read!(p)' DOES bind. A multi-clause defp binds ONE CLAUSE only (b_multi:10 suppressed, b_multi:11 still reported in the same run). Config.CSRF and .heex XSS.Raw are inline-unwaivable for structural reasons read in the source: Config checks never route through combine_skips, and Parse.get_meta_template_funs/1 calls File.read! directly rather than the skip-rewriting read_file/1, so a template's source never sees the substitution.

REFUTED — that fingerprints are toolchain-unstable (security.yml's own stated rationale)

Measured on an identical tree: CI (1.18.1/OTP27) and local (1.19.5/OTP28 — a wider gap than the pinned pair) produced byte-identical 51-finding sets, diff empty. A local regeneration reproduced the CI artifact's 106 entries with 57/57 shared fingerprints identical, 0 differing. Finding.fingerprint/1 is :erlang.phash2([type, vuln_source, filename, vuln_line_no]) — phash2 is portable and the AST comes from Code.string_to_quoted, not the compiler. The line number is IN the hash, which is the actual disease: inserting two lines moved three baselined findings and all three re-reported, while two INLINE-annotated functions in the same file stayed suppressed across the identical shift. The matched-toolchain ceremony buys nothing; the human gate can rest only on review.

PROVEN — the phantom mass is 52 of 108, and the blocking gate cannot see it

Two unrelated methods agree entry-for-entry. Text-anchor resolution: "scanned 100 anchorable baseline entries; 50 stale", EXIT 1. CI's own same-toolchain rescan artifact: baseline_lines=106, sobelow-skips.diff = 52 deletions / 50 additions. The two sets differ by exactly one row — router.ex:2550, a Config.CSRF the text method deliberately skips. Phantoms are INERT rather than loaded guns: a drifted fingerprint matches nothing unless an AST-identical call reappears at the identical line. But that is precisely the collision a refactor produces, with no signal — and the blocking overlap gate is fixture-proven to PASS under both drift and file-move, which is 100% of what this wave migrates. It also PASSES for a file with annotations and zero baseline rows, the janitor's exact case.

The staleness check is buildable and was mutation-proven in four directions: reds on main (50 stale), greens on a cleaned baseline (0 stale), reds again on a SINGLE seeded +1 line shift (health.ex:319 to :320), and exits 2 fail-closed on an empty baseline with "error: ZERO anchorable baseline entries scanned — refusing to report a pass". It runs in about a second with no BEAM, so it can join the blocking job.

FOUND, unhunted — GAP A, proven by execution against a real Postgres

import_member/3 (workspace_bundle.ex:1013) dispatches entry name and entry columns from the uploaded manifest straight into COPY/INSERT with no membership check; table_exists?/1 (:350-353) gates only the DDL passes. A hostile manifest naming schema_migrations returned ok with the row present. One naming users returned USERS_AFTER_ROWS=[["9fe90b32-bc22-4f10-9c1d-ae985ff40971", "attacker@example.com"]] — an attacker-chosen identity row with an attacker-chosen hashed_password, inside the transaction that has already DROPped member FKs and DISABLEd triggers. This violates qi/1's own written invariant at :1141-1143, and table_exists? would be insufficient anyway: existence is not membership, and users exists. A 19-line Catalog-derived guard was prototyped; the adjacent suite ran 237 tests, 0 failures with it applied. No existing test would catch it — all 30-plus workspace_bundle tests build their manifest from a real export and none tampers with tables.

Coverage and not-founds, stated rather than implied

Decisions — D135 through D146, each with its one-line why

These mirror the charter; the charter is the epic's memory and this Paper is the wave's story. Where verification contradicted the direction, the evidence won.

Wave plan — what is in flight while the builders work

Fence: api/**, api/scripts/**, .github/workflows/security.yml, docs/ops/merge-gates.md. Strictly OUT: tenancy/workspace_bundle (D82 plus PR #6551), router.ex (Config.* is unannotatable), and cloud/** plus templates/** (the concurrent Site Spawner wave). api/.sobelow-skips is owned by S1 alone — that is the only reason S5 is round 2; its code is disjoint.

HIGH-FLIP-RISK: S1 — the per-site reachability verdict for each of the 19 findings; a wrong verdict waives a real finding forever, and this wave has already watched one 'genuinely new unreviewed SQL' claim collapse into arithmetic drift and one blanket refutation over-correct. HIGH-FLIP-RISK: S5 — the path-provenance judgment for blobstore/s3.ex, where 10 of 15 findings are NEW code that no baseline ever reviewed, so an inherited verdict would be fabricated. Both warrant a genuinely independent second reviewer before merge; this workflow spawns exactly one, so that dispatch is a manual lead step.

Backlog filed as published epic children: felix-w23-bl-bundle-member-guard (P0, GAP A, fenced to PDS, sequenced after #6551), felix-w23-bl-fenced-sixteen (P1, the 16 findings green depends on), felix-w23-bl-continue-on-error-flip (P2, round 3), felix-w23-bl-overlap-unbound-annotation (P2, nothing gates annotation binding), felix-w23-bl-dataset-slug-format (P3), felix-w23-bl-corpus-gate-integrity (P3).

Cross-epic, stated explicitly rather than absorbed silently: hg-bl-sobelow-fingerprint-to-inline-migration (Honest Gates backlog item 6, open, P2, GH #6403) IS this migration and already owns the continue-on-error criterion verbatim. Felix ADOPTS it by name rather than filing a fourth copy — pds-bl-sobelow-baseline-line-shift-reconcile, its -tenancy sibling, and hg-bl-sobelow-red-under-green are the other three. hg-bl-sobelow-inline-annotation-reversion is closed by content outright: its premise (the reconciler runs --mark-skip-all without --skip) was fixed on main by c69cc0b1e (#6412).

Debrief — Wave 23 built, reviewed, pushed. Grade A−.

All four round-1 slices built green, were reviewed adversarially, had their gates re-run on the reviewer's final state, and are PUSHED with PRs open. Round-2 felix-w23-s5-blobstore-migration is unbuilt BY DESIGN under the sequenced-rounds law — it edits api/.sobelow-skips, which S1 owns exclusively.

DATED CORRECTION 2026-07-28 (review) — the Wave plan's "staleness ratchet in the blocking job" is superseded

The Wave plan section above, and D142, describe S2's staleness check as joining the BLOCKING job. The builder built exactly that and flagged the obvious hazard: it reds on main today (50 stale), so it must merge after S1. Review re-measured and found that warning necessary but NOT sufficient. With S1's pruned baseline AND S1's sources applied together — which is the only honest way to measure it, because S1's added comment lines shift line numbers inside the very files it edits — 31 entries are STILL stale. S1's 19 deletions do not clear the check.

What the reviewer independently re-derived, rather than re-read

STILL OWED: a genuinely INDEPENDENT second reviewer on S1's per-site reachability verdicts. This workflow spawns exactly one reviewer, so that dispatch is a manual lead step. S5, when it is built, carries the same obligation and a harder version of it — 10 of its 15 findings are new code no baseline ever reviewed.

On the wish's standing sore — stated plainly

Main's Sobelow could NOT be made honest without a human gate this wave, and the wave now knows why in two independent senses rather than one. S3 proved that even a fully drained baseline cannot make Sobelow block a merge: SR-1 is live and stage S4 excludes every check in a paths-filtered workflow, proven by the blocking mix-audit job being excluded too. S2's ratchet measured that the baseline itself is 50 dead promises out of 100 checkable rows — 31 after S1. The sore is real, it is now MEASURED and INSTRUMENTED, and it is not closed. Saying so is the improvement-only doctrine working.

Ledger audit

Honest across all four slices: 4/5 criteria stamped with real evidence as the builders worked, the merge-gated criterion left open for the lead, lifecycle in_progress on every one. S5 is correctly open and unclaimed at 0/5. No task outside this wave was touched.

Grade: A−

What earns it. Every slice named its failure mode or quoted its measurement, which is the epic's whole doctrine, and three of the four are proven by mutation rather than by assertion. S1 is the strongest piece of work in the wave: the empty-baseline twin scan is the only proof shape that can catch a D141(c) waiver transfer, the builder chose it unprompted, and an independent re-run reproduced it to the entry. S1 also refused an obvious trap — it kept the renditions.ex:107 row because that one still RESOLVES, so deleting it would have re-reddened a live finding. S3 replaced two wrong numbers and one unsatisfiable precondition with re-derived, command-quoted facts, and found the discriminating proof (the blocking mix-audit job excluded too) rather than the merely-consistent one. S4 removed a genuinely vacuous assertion and then proved the replacement can fail. Bloat is near zero: no speculative refactor, no aesthetic churn, and one slice's honest conclusion was to KEEP a row rather than ship a bigger delta.

What holds it back. S2 shipped a gate that would have reddened every PR in the repository, and its own builder's mitigation — merge after S1 — does not work, because the arithmetic of its interaction with S1 was never computed. That is a measurement the slice's own doctrine demanded and did not take, on the exact axis the slice is about. Two smaller things: S1's validation.ex verdict rests on 'every current call site passes a literal' with nothing enforcing it, an honest but unguarded waiver; and S3 read sobelow's source for the floor-of-10 claim rather than planting an annotation above a Config.CSRF pipeline and watching it be ignored, which this repo's own make-the-check-able-to-fail doctrine rates higher. None of these is fatal, and none was hidden — all three appear in the builders' own reviews, which is itself worth something.

What the next wave should take

Merge order is load-bearing: S1 (#6616) first, because S2's ratchet reads the baseline S1 prunes; then S2 (#6617), S3 (#6618), S4 (#6619), and the charter entry (#6620) in any order. The lead closes the merge-gated criterion on each slice task. Then dispatch felix-w23-s5-blobstore-migration — 15 findings, 10 of them new S3-cache code no baseline ever reviewed, HIGH-FLIP-RISK on path provenance, and owed an independent second reviewer. After S5 the staleness residue drops to roughly 16, at which point felix-w23-bl-staleness-blocking-flip is the single row that converts the new ratchet from a report into a gate — and that is the first time in this epic that 'Sobelow is honest on main' becomes a claim anyone can make without a human gate.
description: Wave 23 of the felix-pristine epic. Main's Sobelow job has been red for five-plus days and the diagnosis was wrong: not toolchain fingerprint drift but a line-anchored baseline that both reds forever and silently waives what moved into its place — hiding 12 never-reviewed raw-SQL sites. The wave migrates the class to durable inline annotations, triages every finding on its merits, and ratchets the gate so it cannot go blind again.
